task.title: Configuring read-only mode for standalone Red Hat Quay
task.shortdesc: To put a standalone Red Hat Quay deployment into read-only mode, you can add the service key files and REGISTRY_STATE settings to your configuration bundle and restart Quay.

ul.li: You have created the service keys and added them to your PostgreSQL database.

context.p: After the service keys have been created and added to your PostgreSQL database, you must restart the Quay container on your standalone deployment.

After starting Red Hat Quay, a banner inside your instance informs users that Red Hat Quay is running in read-only mode. Pushes should be rejected and a 405 error should be logged. You can test this by running the following command:

info.codeblock: 613be09ab3c0: Preparing denied: System is currently read-only. Pulls will succeed but all write operations are currently suspended.
info.p: With your Red Hat Quay deployment on read-only mode, you can safely manage your registry’s operations and perform such actions as backup and restore.
